name: billing-bkash-merchant

envVars.BKASH_MERCHANT_APP_KEY: The app key of your bKash merchant account, from https://developer.bka.sh for the sandbox and from bKash's merchant onboarding for live. Required once BILLING_PROVIDER=bkash-merchant. Every tutorial calls this BKASH_APP_KEY; the MERCHANT segment keeps it clear of billing-bkash-personal's keys when both modules are on disk. Unset, every checkout throws BillingError("invalid_request") naming this key before anything is sent.
envVars.BKASH_MERCHANT_APP_SECRET: The app secret issued with the app key. Required once BILLING_PROVIDER=bkash-merchant. It is sent on the token grant and the token refresh, so a deployed Worker must hold it as a secret (`wrangler secret put BKASH_MERCHANT_APP_SECRET`), never in wrangler.jsonc.
envVars.BKASH_MERCHANT_USERNAME: The merchant API username, sent as the `username` header on the two token calls. Required once BILLING_PROVIDER=bkash-merchant. It is not your bKash wallet number and not your portal login.
envVars.BKASH_MERCHANT_PASSWORD: The merchant API password that goes with the username, sent as the `password` header on the two token calls. Required, and a Worker secret for the same reason the app secret is.
envVars.BKASH_MERCHANT_MODE: Which gateway host to use: `live` for https://tokenized.pay.bka.sh, anything else for the sandbox at https://tokenized.sandbox.bka.sh. Optional, and it fails safe — only the exact string `live` selects the live gateway, so a typo sends a test payment to the sandbox rather than a real one to production.

removeWarnings: Removing this module does not cancel anything at bKash, and there is nothing to cancel: this provider stores no instrument and nothing recurs at the gateway. Subjects simply stop being asked to pay.
The stored gateway token stays in your kv store under the `billing:bkash-merchant:token` key until it expires. Delete it if you are rotating the app key.
If you handed bKash support a webhook listener URL during onboarding, ask them to remove it. Otherwise bKash keeps posting to an endpoint that now answers 404.

`@repo/kv` stays in packages/billing/package.json, as every package-json-dependency patch does. Removing a dependency is yours to do; drop it with `pnpm remove` in that workspace once nothing else there imports it.
